back: An organisation of workers that represents them to protect and improve pay, conditions and job security.
Negotiation between employers and workers' representatives over pay, hours and conditions, leading to an agreement for a group.
A neutral person helps management and workers to talk and reach their own agreement; no decision is imposed.
An independent person hears both sides and gives a decision that both have agreed to accept.
Strike, go-slow, work-to-rule and overtime ban (by workers); lock-out (by employers).
Fewer disputes, higher productivity and quality, lower absence and turnover, flexibility and a good reputation.
Works councils, workers' committees, union representatives, suggestion schemes and worker directors.
Preparation, establishing the environment, exploring needs, testing understanding, negotiating a position, reaching agreement.
Compare the cost of the settlement with the cost of conflict, share information, use conciliation first and offer non-pay benefits where possible.
